company: Region Group (formerly Shopping Centres Australasia Property Group, ASX: SCA)
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: REIT Personnel
tiers.description: Each director, officer and employee of the REIT, and each contractor and consultant whose terms of engagement apply the Policy to them. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, short-term dealing rule, blackout periods and the hardship clearance notice regime.

tiers.name: Designated Person
tiers.description: Each director of the REIT, the Company Secretary, the General Counsel, other key management personnel, and any other REIT Person designated by the General Counsel and Company Secretary. Subject to additional notification and approval, reporting, margin lending and Connected Person obligations under section 4.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Family members expected to influence or be influenced by the REIT Person, business partners, and companies, trustees or entities the REIT Person is a director/chief executive of, is a beneficiary of, or controls. Designated Persons must ensure their Connected Persons observe the notification and approval procedure (via the Designated Person) and do not deal during a blackout period or engage in short-term dealing.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant REIT Units

windows.end_anchor: 12 noon (AEST) on the next business day after the day on which the half-year results are released
12 noon (AEST) on the next business day after the day on which full year results are released

windows.start_anchor: six weeks before the AGM of the REIT
windows.end_anchor: 12 noon (AEST) on the next business day after the day on which the AGM of the REIT is held

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The REIT (at the discretion of its directors) may declare a blackout period during which REIT Personnel are prohibited from Dealing in REIT Units at any time, at its absolute discretion and without prior notice; the Policy does not address whether the fact or reason for such a blackout is kept confidential.

rules.detail: REIT Personnel must not use, nor allow to be used, any Derivatives (including collars) in relation to unvested REIT Units.
rules.evidence: REIT Personnel must not use, nor allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any unvested REIT Units or vested REIT Units that are still subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Derivatives are also banned over vested REIT Units that remain subject to disposal restrictions.
rules.evidence: REIT Personnel must not use, nor allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any unvested REIT Units or vested REIT Units that are still subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: For non-designated REIT Personnel, use of Derivatives over vested and exercisable REIT Units must comply with the law and other provisions of the Policy (short-term dealing rule, blackout periods) but does not require notification or approval.
rules.evidence: The use of Derivatives over REIT Units that have vested and are exercisable must, like any other Dealing in REIT Units, comply with the law and other provisions of this Policy, including in relation to short-term dealings, blackout periods and, in the case of Designated Persons, the notification and approval procedures set out in section 4.2.

rules.detail: Designated Persons may use Derivatives (the definition expressly lists collars as an example) over vested, exercisable REIT Units, but must first notify and obtain written approval from the Chairman (or Company Secretary), valid for five business days, and must comply with blackout periods and the short-term dealing rule.
rules.evidence: in the case of Designated Persons, the notification and approval procedures set out in section 4.2

rules.detail: Hedging via any Derivative (defined to include transactions limiting economic risk of holding REIT Units) is banned over unvested Units.
rules.evidence: REIT Personnel must not use, nor allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any unvested REIT Units or vested REIT Units that are still subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Hedging is banned over vested Units still subject to disposal restrictions.
rules.evidence: REIT Personnel must not use, nor allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any unvested REIT Units or vested REIT Units that are still subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not named, but Dealing broadly covers entering into or closing out a transaction and any agreement to do so; for non-designated personnel it is subject only to blackout periods, the short-term rule and the general insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: entering into or closing out; or the entry into any agreement to do any of the above things

rules.detail: For Designated Persons, a monetisation arrangement is caught by the broad Dealing definition and requires prior notification and written approval from the Chairman before it can proceed.
rules.evidence: Any Designated Person must, prior to Dealing in REIT Units (subject to certain limited exceptions set out below), first notify the Chairman

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named and is not included in the Dealing definition.

CFDs are not named but fall within the Derivatives definition's catch-all for any transaction in financial products limiting the economic risk of holding REIT Units, so they are banned over unvested Units on the same basis as other derivatives.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant REIT Units

rules.detail: A CFD over vested, unrestricted REIT Units is treated as a Derivative and permitted for Designated Persons subject to prior notification and approval.
rules.evidence: in the case of Designated Persons, the notification and approval procedures set out in section 4.2

rules.detail: Outright ban on Designated Persons entering margin lending arrangements with respect to REIT Units.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not enter into margin lending arrangements with respect to REIT Units.

rules.detail: The margin lending ban in section 4.6 is expressed only in relation to Designated Persons; it is not addressed for other REIT Personnel.

The margin lending ban is limited to arrangements properly described as margin lending and does not extend to other loan arrangements or instruments secured by a security interest over REIT Units; Designated Persons may grant such security but must first notify the Chairman of their intention and disclose the terms.
rules.evidence: This restriction is limited to arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements and does not extend to other types of loan arrangements or instruments which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of REIT Units. Designated Persons may enter into or acquire such other types of loan arrangements or instruments, but only after first notifying the Chairman of their intention to do so and disclosing the terms of such loan arrangements or instruments.

rules.detail: Non-margin secured loan arrangements over REIT Units are permitted for Designated Persons, conditional on first notifying the Chairman of the intention to enter the arrangement and disclosing its terms; Designated Persons should confirm the characterisation with the Company Secretary if uncertain.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may enter into or acquire such other types of loan arrangements or instruments, but only after first notifying the Chairman of their intention to do so and disclosing the terms of such loan arrangements or instruments.

rules.detail: Section 4.6 addresses only Designated Persons; secured financing by other REIT Personnel is not addressed.

No REIT Person may deal in REIT Units within 12 months of their acquisition unless they first resign. Vesting or exercise of options/rights under an incentive scheme, and the subsequent sale of the underlying units within 12 months, is not prohibited, nor is a sale at the end of a restriction period under such a scheme.
rules.evidence: no REIT Person may deal in REIT Units within 12 months of their acquisition by that REIT Person unless they first resign.

clearance.approver: Chairman (or, if the Designated Person is the Chairman, the Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (or, if the Designated Person is the Company Secretary, the Chief Executive Officer)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable and, in any case, no more than 2 days after the Dealing
clearance.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in the proposed Dealing until the Chairman (or Company Secretary, as applicable) has approved the proposed Dealing in writing. Any such approval is valid for five business days, or such other period specified in it

clearance.approver: Chairman (or, if the applicant is the Chairman, the Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly after the sale is completed
clearance.evidence: A clearance notice allowing a REIT Person who is not in possession of Inside Information to sell (but not purchase) REIT Units during the periods described in section 3.2 above may be given by the REIT where that REIT Person is in severe financial hardship or there are other exceptional circumstances.

clearance.approver: Chairman/Company Secretary, via the Designated Person
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, via the Designated Person
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no more than 2 days after the Dealing
clearance.evidence: request their Connected Persons to observe the notification and approval procedure outlined in section 4.2 above by giving the Designated Person the information necessary for the Designated Person to lodge notices and requests in respect of the Connected Person's dealings in REIT Units

carve_outs: Vesting or exercise of options over or rights to REIT Units under an incentive scheme, and the subsequent sale of the underlying units within a 12 month period
Sale of REIT Units at the end of a restriction period applying under such a scheme
short_term.evidence: no REIT Person may deal in REIT Units within 12 months of their acquisition by that REIT Person unless they first resign. Subject to sections 3.2 and 3.4 of this Policy, this prohibition does not restrict the vesting or exercise of options over or rights to REIT Units under an incentive scheme

exceptions.evidence: A clearance notice allowing a REIT Person who is not in possession of Inside Information to sell (but not purchase) REIT Units during the periods described in section 3.2 above may be given by the REIT where that REIT Person is in severe financial hardship
exceptional circumstances would include passive trades, for instance where a person is required by a court order or otherwise by law to sell the relevant REIT Units

transfers of REIT Units that are already held by the REIT Person or in which the REIT Person has a relevant interest into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the REIT Person is the beneficiary
transfers of REIT Units between a REIT Person and a Connected Person

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in REIT Units) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a REIT Person is a trustee, trading in the REIT Units by that trust provided that the REIT Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during the blackout period is taken by the other trustee(s) or by the investment managers independently of the REIT Person
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or scheme of arrangement in respect of the REIT

dealing in REIT Units under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board of the REIT
applying for REIT Units, and acquiring REIT Units under such application, under any employee share plan in which a REIT Person has been invited to participate

acquiring REIT Units under a distribution reinvestment plan or unit purchase plan operated by the REIT, where the REIT Person did not enter into the plan or amend the terms of their participation in the plan during the blackout period

a disposal of REIT Units that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement

dealing under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with the procedures set out in this policy and where ... the trading plan does not permit the REIT Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when or whether to trade
dealings where the beneficial interest in the REIT Units does not change

This clause 4 shall not operate to restrict Dealings in REIT Units by a REIT of which a Designated Person acts as trustee if: the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust; the decision to deal ... is taken without reference to, and independently of, the Designated Person; and the Designated Person is not the sole trustee of the trust.

financing_disclosure: Designated Persons: before entering a non-margin loan arrangement or instrument secured by REIT Units, notify the Chairman of the intention to do so and disclose its terms (section 4.6).

exemption_authority: Chairman (or Company Secretary if the Chairman is the applicant) has sole discretion to determine whether severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances exist and to issue a clearance notice permitting a sale (not a purchase) during a blackout period; such sales remain subject to the insider trading prohibition. The REIT's directors may separately impose additional blackout periods at absolute discretion and without prior notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may enter into or acquire such other types of loan arrangements or instruments, but only after first notifying the Chairman of their intention to do so and disclosing the terms of such loan arrangements or instruments.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on vested REIT Units for a funded collar is not banned outright (only 'margin lending arrangements' are), but the Designated Person must pre-notify the Chairman and disclose the loan's terms, and should confirm with the Company Secretary that the facility is not in substance a margin loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Additionally, the REIT may publicly disclose any Derivative positions over REIT Units taken out by a director of the REIT.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's collar position may be publicly disclosed by the REIT at its discretion, a confidentiality consideration for the executive and the bank when structuring the trade.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lender forced sale not excluded from blackout
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of REIT Units that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A secured (non-margin) lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the blackout restriction, but this carve-out is unavailable if the facility is characterised as margin lending, so the loan should be structured and documented as a non-margin secured facility to preserve the bank's ability to enforce during a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly names 'collars' as a type of Derivative, so an equity collar is squarely subject to the section 3.5 vesting-state restrictions and, for Designated Persons, the notification and approval procedure.

summary: A funded collar is achievable for a Designated Person over fully vested, unrestricted REIT Units, subject to conditions. The put and call legs are a 'Derivative' (the Policy expressly names collars as an example) and are permitted for Designated Persons only with prior written notification to and approval from the Chairman, valid for five business days, outside the closed periods, and only while not in possession of Inside Information; derivatives over unvested or still-restricted (holding-locked) units are banned outright. The loan leg cannot be a 'margin lending arrangement' (banned for Designated Persons), but other secured loan arrangements over REIT Units are expressly permitted provided the Designated Person first notifies the Chairman of the intention and discloses the loan's terms. A secured (non-margin) lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the blackout-period restriction, supporting the bank's ability to enforce outside a trading window, but this carve-out does not extend to margin lending arrangements, so the facility should be documented and characterised as a non-margin secured loan. Overall, execution is possible but is gated by vesting state, trading-window timing, Chairman approval/notification, and careful avoidance of margin-lending characterisation.
